open.speaker: cook
lines: Kitchen's closed to customers. You're customers.
Marlene said talk to you. Marlene says a lot of things on the late shift, and I'm the one scraping the grill.
Grill's clean. He scraped it an hour ago.

passives.line: He's holding the spatula edge up. Not a threat. A man who wants something in his hand.
He said her name soft and everything else hard. Twenty-odd years of late shifts beside her.

static.line: He's standing between you and the bin. He's stood between everybody and that bin for years. Go around him.

options.text: We're not here for the grill.

fail.line: Long enough. Longer than your interest, mister.

options.text: (Wait by the bin and say nothing.)

grill.speaker: cook
lines: No. You're here for her. Everybody's here for her once, and then they laugh and go, and I'm the one here after.
Say what you want and say it quick.

years.speaker: cook
lines: Since '71. Rosie hired me off a towboat. Marlene was here before me and she'll be here after, checking that door.
...You listened to her. All the way through. Cal at the register said you did.
He's been waiting to hear that someone did.

wait.speaker: cook
lines: (He slides the bin a foot toward you with his boot and goes back to the grill.)
That's the kindest thing anyone's done in this kitchen tonight.

hub.speaker: cook
lines: You've got till the next order.

options.text: Dwight Mason comes in Thursdays. What does he order?
You've kept her secret longer than she has.
The two men asked her red or red-orange. You heard it.

special.speaker: cook
lines: Meatloaf. Been meatloaf on a Wednesday since Rosie. You want it or you want to stand there?
...Fine. One slice, on the house, 'cause you asked. Sit down and don't tell Marlene.
I'm never not going to tell Marlene.

dwight.speaker: cook
lines: Coffee. Black. Four of 'em, and he drinks the one. Been doing it since before I was here.
Rosie told me never to clear the other three till he's gone. I never asked why. You didn't ask Rosie.
Four coffees. Same as the check from 1966.

dwight_fail.speaker: cook
lines: He orders what he orders and pays what he owes, which is more than you've done tonight.
Cal's got the register. Ask Cal. Cal likes talking.

secret.speaker: cook
lines: ...She wasn't at her sister's. She was out at the plant with Dwight, and I've known since that night, 'cause I'm the one she called.
From the gatehouse. Twenty to three. 'Vern, don't tell Rosie.' I didn't. Rosie's dead and I still ain't.
That's the check in the bin. His number on the back. She keeps it where she can't see it and can't throw it out.
Twenty to three. That's the dispatch log, to the minute.

secret_fail.speaker: cook
lines: You want her secrets, go sit at her counter and ask her to her face, and watch her hands while you do it.

passives.line: That was the right read and the wrong mouth. He'd have told her. He won't tell you.

suits_heard.speaker: cook
lines: I heard. Red or red-orange, like they were ordering paint. She said red. The tall one wrote it down. The other one didn't blink.
They left a twenty on a four-dollar check and she wouldn't touch it. It's in the register still. Cal won't touch it either.
A new bill, I'd bet. Serial in sequence with whatever they paid Lonnie.
